question:
Statements: E ≥ N < Q ≥ B
Conclusions:
I. N ≤ E
II. B = Q
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
explanation:
Read the chain E ≥ N < Q ≥ B from N to E and from B to Q. A mix of > and < (or ≥ and ≤) between two letters breaks the link.
I: N ≤ E always holds in the chain, so it follows.
II: B = Q can fail (e.g. B = 0, Q = 1 fits every statement), so it does not follow.
Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

Conclusions:

II. Some doors are clocks.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

Conclusion I (No doors is clocks.) fails in at least one possible diagram, so it does not follow.
Conclusion II (Some doors are clocks.) fails in at least one possible diagram, so it does not follow.

Answer: Either conclusion I or II follows.
